title: Primary Sizing Station (truck dump, apron feeder, twin-shaft sizer)
model_title: Primary Sizing Station: Two-Sided Truck Dump, Rock Breaker, Apron Feeder, Twin-Shaft Sizer & Discharge Conveyor

introduction.definition: The primary sizing station is the hand-over point between the mine fleet and the conveyor system. Haul trucks reverse onto two tipping decks and tip into a lined dump hopper; a pedestal rock breaker breaks oversize and bridges without anyone entering the hopper; a heavy apron feeder draws ore out at a controlled rate; a twin-shaft mineral sizer reduces run-of-mine lumps (up to ~1.2–1.5 m) to minus ~200 mm by tension and shear; the sized ore drops onto a sacrificial conveyor that passes a self-cleaning tramp magnet and a metal detector before joining the overland conveyor to the refinery.
applications: Primary sizing of sticky, clayey lateritic bauxite (sizers handle wet clay better than jaw or gyratory crushers)
Buffering truck deliveries so the overland conveyor runs at a steady rate
Removing tramp steel before it can rip the overland belt
key_points: Nominal ~1,300–1,500 t/h, design 1,800 t/h to the overland; feeder and sizer rated ~2,000–2,400 t/h for truck surges
ROM top size ~1.2–1.5 m → product –200 mm
Two-sided tipping so two trucks can tip at once

Wheel-stop bunds at least half the wheel height of the largest machine using the dump (~1.35 m for the 2.7 m truck tyres, ~1.55 m here because the loader also tips; the loader tips with its front tyres at the bund — a dedicated loader tip point with a thinner bund set closer to the edge is preferred)
Sizer shafts turn slowly (~50–100 rpm) with high torque; fluid couplings protect the drives
Magnet + metal detector protect the overland belt from bucket teeth and drill steel

introduction.summary: The primary sizing station turns run-of-mine bauxite into a conveyable product. Haul trucks tip from two sides into a lined dump hopper; a pedestal rock breaker deals with oversize; an apron feeder draws ore out at a controlled rate into a twin-shaft mineral sizer that reduces lumps up to ~1.2–1.5 m to minus ~200 mm; the product drops onto a sacrificial conveyor that passes under a self-cleaning tramp magnet and a metal detector before the overland conveyor.

interfaces: Fed by 01-HT haul trucks (and 01-FL loader from the ROM pad)
Discharges to the A02 field / overland conveyor

what_to_look_for: A truck reverses to the wheel-stop bund on the green light and tips ~90 t into the dump hopper; the rock-box ledges take the impact.
The hopper buffers 2–3 truck loads; a pedestal rock breaker breaks any oversize or bridged ore from its cabin above.
The apron feeder pans drag ore out under the hopper at a VFD-controlled speed matched to the sizer and conveyor.

steps.text: A truck reverses to the wheel-stop bund on the green light and tips ~90 t into the dump hopper; the rock-box ledges take the impact.
The hopper buffers 2–3 truck loads; a pedestal rock breaker breaks any oversize or bridged ore from its cabin above.
The apron feeder pans drag ore out under the hopper at a VFD-controlled speed matched to the sizer and conveyor.

The two sizer shafts counter-rotate slowly, turning inward at the top; their horn teeth grip lumps and snap them in tension and shear, the scroll pattern moves oversize along, and lumps that pass the first nip are snapped against the breaker bar beneath the shafts (third stage).
Sized ore (–200 mm) falls through the discharge chute onto the impact beds of the sacrificial conveyor, which runs in a trench under the sizer and then climbs at 12°.
The overband magnet lifts tramp steel off the belt into a chute; the metal detector stops the belt for anything non-magnetic (e.g. broken manganese-steel pans or hammer tools) or missed.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Sizer capacity rises with shaft speed and shaft length; product top size is set by tooth/ring spacing and the gap to the breaker bar and grows as teeth wear; feeder speed is controlled to keep the sizer evenly loaded within motor power and the overland design rate.

civil_works: MSE or RC walls retaining the tipping decks; dump pocket designed for truck impact; drainage of the pocket floor; wheel-stop bunds and lighting.
mechanical_installation: Sizer on a massive foundation with drive bases; shafts and drives aligned (laser); apron feeder levelled with chain tension set; conveyor aligned and belt trained.
Overhead crane or monorail (~20–30 t) and lay-down area for shaft and pan change-outs.
commissioning: No-load runs: rotation, vibration, bearing temperatures; interlock tests (pull-wires, belt drift, blocked chute, metal detector trip, emergency stops).
Load ramp-up with ROM; set feeder speed control to sizer power/conveyor load; test the tramp magnet and metal detector with test pieces.

routine.task: Belt walk: spillage, idlers, belt damage, skirts; test metal detector.
Check hopper level and bridging; inspect rock-breaker tool.

periodic.task: Measure sizer tooth height and hardface or replace tips.
Apron-feeder pan, chain and roller inspection.
Gearbox oil analysis; fluid-coupling oil level.

overhaul.task: Shaft change-out with the crane (spare shafts kept rebuilt).
Pan and chain replacement; liner replacement.

lubrication: Sizer bearings by automatic grease/oil system; feeder head/tail bearings and chains; gearboxes by oil level and analysis.

causes: Tramp steel or a very hard block
remedies: Auto-reverse cycle; remove tramp with isolation; tune feeder speed control

symptoms: No flow with material in the hopper
remedies: Rock breaker; keep the hopper cycling; never enter the hopper
Splice/repair; check magnet and detector sensitivity

items.problem: Truck over-run at the tipping edge
symptoms: Truck strikes or mounts the bund
remedies: Maintain bunds ≥ half tyre height, lighting, traffic lights and spotting rules

safety: Tipping decks: traffic lights, bund height, spotting rules, CCTV.
No tipping while the rock breaker is working; breaker exclusion zone for fragments.
Hopper and sizer are confined spaces with engulfment and crush hazards — isolation, permit, never enter a live hopper.
Conveyor guarding and pull-wire emergency stops along the belt; lock-out before belt cleaning or idler change.
Dust: sprays at the hopper, hoods at the sizer discharge.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Primary Sizing Station (truck dump, apron feeder, twin-shaft sizer).
Belt walk: spillage, idlers, belt damage, skirts; test metal detector.
Check hopper level and bridging; inspect rock-breaker tool.
Measure sizer tooth height and hardface or replace tips.
Apron-feeder pan, chain and roller inspection.
Shaft change-out with the crane (spare shafts kept rebuilt).
Pan and chain replacement; liner replacement.
Watch for sizer jam / stall: motor current trip. Common cause: tramp steel or a very hard block.
Watch for oversize product: lumps > 200 mm on the belt. Common cause: worn tooth tips.
Watch for hopper bridging / hang-up: no flow with material in the hopper. Common cause: sticky clayey ore, wet season.
Record every inspection so trends — wear, temperatures, pressures, leaks and performance — can be compared over time.

questions.question: Why is a twin-shaft sizer chosen for lateritic bauxite instead of a jaw crusher?
options: It handles sticky, clayey wet ore and breaks by tension/shear with less fines and no packing
questions.explanation: Sizers cope with sticky ROM and give a controlled top size.

questions.question: What does the apron feeder do?
options: Draws ore out of the hopper at a controlled rate and takes the dumping impact off the sizer
questions.explanation: Apron feeders are robust, controllable feeders under dump hoppers.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the wheel-stop bund?
options: To stop a reversing truck going over the edge — at least half the wheel height of the largest machine using the dump
questions.explanation: Bunds ≥ half tyre height are standard practice.

questions.question: Why are fluid couplings fitted in the sizer drives?
options: Soft start and slip on overload/jam, protecting the drive train

questions.question: Which device lifts tramp steel off the belt?
questions.explanation: The magnet removes ferrous tramp; the detector trips the belt for the rest.

questions.question: Who may enter the dump hopper to clear a bridge?
options: Nobody while it is live — use the rock breaker; entry only under isolation and confined-space permit
questions.explanation: Hopper entry is a high-risk confined space with engulfment hazard.

questions.question: The sizer product size is –200 mm because…
options: It suits the 1,200 mm overland belt and its transfer chutes (lump ≤ about 1/5–1/6 of belt width with fines)
questions.explanation: CEMA lump-size guidance and chute clearances limit top size; the refinery does its own secondary crushing and grinding.

controls: Control-room or local HMI: feeder speed (VFD), sizer start/stop/reverse, conveyor sequence, magnet on/off, rock-breaker joysticks, traffic lights
pre_start: Inspect tipping decks and bunds, hopper level, guards, pull-wires; test metal detector
start_up: Confirm the A02 overland is running (permissive), dust sprays on
Magnet energised and metal detector healthy → discharge conveyor → sizer (inward rotation) → apron feeder at minimum speed; then green lights
normal: Keep the hopper partly full (protects the pans); trim feeder speed to sizer power and conveyor load
Break oversize promptly; watch sizer current and product top size
Respond to metal-detector trips: find and remove the metal before restart
shut_down: Red lights; leave at least ~1 truck load in the hopper to protect the pans (empty it only for liner/pan work)
Stop the feeder → sizer runs empty ~30–60 s → stop the sizer → belt runs empty → stop the conveyor → de-energise the magnet; isolate
alarms_interlocks: A02 overland stop → 01-CV-001 stop → sizer stop → feeder stop (sequence interlock)
Sizer stall/overload → feeder stop, auto-reverse (2–3 attempts) then trip and alarm
Zero-speed switches on the feeder tail shaft and sizer shafts; sizer bearing temperature/vibration
Blocked-chute probes at the sizer discharge and head chute; belt rip detector; metal detector → belt stop + marker spray
Belt drift, speed (slip) and pull-wire trips
Rock breaker active / hopper high level → tipping lights red; hopper low level → alarm and slow the feeder to keep a protective layer
tips: Never let the hopper run empty — trucks then tip straight onto the pans
Tip on both decks alternately to spread wear
